item.title: SCP-5366: Hmm... Is this related to a Forgotten Trope of Europe?
item.content:encoded:
Or Strange Minds Think Alike… Cool either way, but historical backing makes it cooler.

https://tvtropes.org/Main/ForgottenTrope

Older Than Steam:

Excessive mourning wakes the dead: The belief that excessive mourning disturbs the dead's rest was a fairly common superstition in Europe from the Middle Ages to about the eighteenth century. That's why English has the term 'wake' in the first place.

  • “The Unquiet Grave” is an English ballad sung from the perspective of a person note who mourns their dead lover for A Year and a Day. The lover then comes back as a ghost to haunt them, and begs the singer to stop mourning so they can have peace in the afterlife.
  • The Shroud is one of the fairy tales collected by The Brothers Grimm. The story is about a woman who weeps over her dead son day and night. One night, the boy's ghost asks her to stop mourning so he can rest in death.

item.title: SCP-166:
item.content:encoded:
Eh, while a touchy subject I think people should grow a thicker skin, particularly as is was not graphic in any way.

And if it needs to go because a new site policy says "NO". Then, fine, remove it. Slap a Big old [SEALED by O5 Council] on SCP-166s page (or the ethics committee, I love that story about them actually outranking O5)

Adjusting it like this is just confusing, and obviously tied the writers hands, where he had to still incorporate the original as much as possible instead of making a new interesting SCP. (and broke the vote counter, and why is there scp-0166 as well?)

Which is a shame because the potential is there, but as a rewrite it lacks depth.
What about testing on humans? animals(kitten pet turns into saber tooth anyone?) What is this instinctive knowledge of a global ritual, was she interviewed regarding it? Any info breaches by other organizations looking for it or near misses? Is there concerns that "the Goddess" spawned other children?

Interesting stuff is there but instead it feels like a lazy Frankenstein of an article.

item.title: SCP-5510:
item.content:encoded:
These kinds of simple artifacts feel like the strongest forces in the SCP universe to me. Founded upon a simple law. SCP-871 duplicates if uneaten. SCP-498's alarm increases 0.4 dB per seconds. SCP-173 moves if you blink. And SCP-5510's pause button stops the world.

I wouldn't be surprised if even gods cannot alter such laws.

item.title: SCP-5245:
item.content:encoded:
I really hope some more experienced critics than me decide to weigh in on this.

As a general note, if a piece is dipping into negative ratings, reviewers may prefer to provide feedback elsewhere so said reviews aren't lost if the author decides to delete the page themselves. Staff running deletions save the feedback given in the announcement thread, but it's often more efficient to have a dedicated thread for discussing how to edit a draft, when there isn't the added pressure of the rating module or deletion timer.

Reviewers who provide feedback on mainsite posts in the negatives are much appreciated, but they're doing a favor more than fulfilling an obligation. Author, you're definitely free to contact reviewers to ask for feedback on this post, but you'll likely get more interest in the chat and forums.

item.title: SCP-5733:

item.title: SCP-5245:
item.content:encoded:
So, I'm seeing the initial downvotes happening, and I can honestly see why. But then I looked in here and saw a lack of anyone commenting alongside, and I wish they would. That's why I'm going to comment myself, even though I normally just passively read on this site.

Through the tonal issues and various other problems I can't quite nail down in words myself, I can see a story here that I like. A desire to return to simpler times, put into practice with unforeseen consequences. An anomaly which was, in a sense, its own first victim, and is gradually becoming aware of this. An artist constrained by the rules of their own creation even as they start to see the flaws - but they're committed now, they can't unmake what was made. A living story written in permanent ink, mistakes and all.

I really wouldn't want to see this concept pass quietly into deletion just because it doesn't "feel like" the modern Foundation. I really hope some more experienced critics than me decide to weigh in on this.
